title: What are you doing this week?
content_html:
1. I just made the leap from ~20 years of engineering and tech to teaching public high school programming. Last week was our first week back and I am just trying to keep my head above water. This week, kicking off three different AP compsci classes. I just couldn’t deal with the horrible confluence of forced LLM usage and corporate culture anymore, so time to pursue some other dreams!

    1. I would love to follow via some blog.

      1. I'd love to hear more about your journey, as I'm considering this path as well once I completely tire of corporate culture. What state (assuming USA because of AP classes) did you make the transition in, and what was required of you?

        1. It was all a bit of a whirlwind- I had decided to quit my job some time in August or September to take the year to work on getting a teaching license and substitute teaching. A computer science position suddenly opened up at my local high school, so in the span of 8 days I went from responding to the posting to onboarding.

          This is in Massachusetts, the main requirement was at least 5 years of professional SWE experience. This position is part of the vocational experience- now referred to as Career and Technical Education (CTE), so real world creds >> teaching license. The expectation is that some time this year I get my Chapter 74 license (special CTE variant of teaching license), which looks very straightforward (it’s mostly just SWE stuff you would know working already).

          MA also recently enacted a new “alternative pathway to teaching” which allows a STEM masters degree to substitute for some of the core teaching license requirements, so that is helping me out too.

      2. Staying far away from work and the computer by spending one week in the beatiful Estonian capital, Tallinn and its surroundings.

        It is quite a change of pace compared to Budapest, in no small part because Estonia as a whole has less people than that city.

        1. Watched Nolan's Tenet yesterday, crux of the plot happens in the city

        2. Canadian amateur radio operator exam (Basic) on Thursday - so far passing all the practice tests with 85+! Studied "hard" for about 2 months, but before that, I had to retry actually starting studying many times throughout the past year (starting with regulations is bo-ring). Already got my sights on the VE2LKF callsign :D (my name as initials). Could be cool to start a lobste.rs HF digital radio club...

          Trying to finish up an article on "AI" too (in quotations, because it's more general than just AI). This is writing from a historical approach, trying to understand my current feelings and how the people of the past felt and how we may need to continue shifting our feelings on the matter. No AI was used in the writing of it in any capacity, and I say that to give respect to my readers and demonstrate great effort that went into the piece and hopefully the words will retain their weight.

          1. I got my entry-level license earlier this year, and I literally just downloaded the application form for the advanced-level exam here in Croatia. I finally got on air this summer, and it's loads of fun. Living in an apartment building downtown isn't doing wonders for the amount of time I'm able to tinker with it, but that's a challenge in its own right & I'm working on it.

            A digital net of crustaceans sounds neat! I'm not sure how that might look like, but I'm all in. :)

            Best of luck with the exam! 73 de 9A3NPX

          2. I'm about to head out for a long bike ride since we have a 3 day weekend Labor Day weekend.

            Tomorrow is back to work, and I'm going to look at some bugs in our Catia importer.

            1. Enjoying the 3d weekend for the US, then prepping tasks and logistics and other code-based prep work for taking a small team to Reykjavik the following week for an offsite work week!

              1. For work:

                I am working on a b2b prototype for Thetix (https://thetix.ai) with a design partner. Also trying to have conversations with more folks. Better have conversations than spend time building something nobody wants.

                For fun/research:

                I am building a shared workspace feature for Abject (https://abject.world) so that a team of people can share a workspace and work on a shared project.

                I'm also working on two different kind of coding agents, both testing different werid ideas. One is uslmax which builds off my blog here (https://blog.mempko.com/a-million-kakapos/). The other is called turboagent which is testing another wacky idea (I'll open source if it turns out it's not crap). Also uses Raku (https://raku.org/) which is a bit strange.

                1. been spinning the wheels in my head about an essay about broader cultural trends due to LLMs, with reference to the really thought provoking book Otaku: Japan's Database Animals by Hiroki Azuma. Roughly something about how the customer-facing chatbots are "database replicants", reassembling culture out of preexisting parts in a way that is appealing to database animals... Or something like that.

                  Otherwise, getting back into writing Haskell after doing zero programming for the past two years. Finishing up Pnin probably, maybe starting in on some Faulkner if my LoA order comes in... Or Libra by Delillo which has been calling my name for months.

                  1. Trying to make progress on an adaptive learning scheduler that guides practice sessions for technical piano exercises. Kind of like spaced repetition for scales and arpeggios.

                    1. In no particular order:

                      • Solving a weird bug in a platform I'm maintaining, been chasing this one for the last couple of days.
                      • Writing an article about a recent RubyConf talk by Dave Thomas.
                      • Preparing boards of ash wood that I'm going to use for the floor of the studio I'm building next to our house.
                      • Hopefully I'll have enough time to do some paperwork and accounting for my business before the weekend.

                      1. Making myself an n-body simulator with stellular evolution along with other celestial objects.

1. I just made the leap from ~20 years of engineering and tech to teaching public high school programming. Last week was our first week back and I am just trying to keep my head above water. This week, kicking off three different AP compsci classes. I just couldn’t deal with the horrible confluence of forced LLM usage and corporate culture anymore, so time to pursue some other dreams! I would love to follow via some blog. I'd love to hear more about your journey, as I'm considering this path as well once I completely tire of corporate culture. What state (assuming USA because of AP classes) did you make the transition in, and what was required of you? It was all a bit of a whirlwind- I had decided to quit my job some time in August or September to take the year to work on getting a teaching license and substitute teaching. A computer science position suddenly opened up at my local high school, so in the span of 8 days I went from responding to the posting to onboarding. This is in Massachusetts, the main requirement was at least 5 years of professional SWE experience. This position is part of the vocational experience- now referred to as Career and Technical Education (CTE), so real world creds >> teaching license. The expectation is that some time this year I get my Chapter 74 license (special CTE variant of teaching license), which looks very straightforward (it’s mostly just SWE stuff you would know working already). MA also recently enacted a new “alternative pathway to teaching” which allows a STEM masters degree to substitute for some of the core teaching license requirements, so that is helping me out too.
  2. Staying far away from work and the computer by spending one week in the beatiful Estonian capital, Tallinn and its surroundings. It is quite a change of pace compared to Budapest, in no small part because Estonia as a whole has less people than that city. Watched Nolan's Tenet yesterday, crux of the plot happens in the city
  3. Canadian amateur radio operator exam (Basic) on Thursday - so far passing all the practice tests with 85+! Studied "hard" for about 2 months, but before that, I had to retry actually starting studying many times throughout the past year (starting with regulations is bo-ring). Already got my sights on the VE2LKF callsign :D (my name as initials). Could be cool to start a lobste.rs HF digital radio club... Trying to finish up an article on "AI" too (in quotations, because it's more general than just AI). This is writing from a historical approach, trying to understand my current feelings and how the people of the past felt and how we may need to continue shifting our feelings on the matter. No AI was used in the writing of it in any capacity, and I say that to give respect to my readers and demonstrate great effort that went into the piece and hopefully the words will retain their weight. I got my entry-level license earlier this year, and I literally just downloaded the application form for the advanced-level exam here in Croatia. I finally got on air this summer, and it's loads of fun. Living in an apartment building downtown isn't doing wonders for the amount of time I'm able to tinker with it, but that's a challenge in its own right & I'm working on it. A digital net of crustaceans sounds neat! I'm not sure how that might look like, but I'm all in. :) Best of luck with the exam! 73 de 9A3NPX
  4. I'm about to head out for a long bike ride since we have a 3 day weekend Labor Day weekend. Tomorrow is back to work, and I'm going to look at some bugs in our Catia importer.
  5. Enjoying the 3d weekend for the US, then prepping tasks and logistics and other code-based prep work for taking a small team to Reykjavik the following week for an offsite work week!
